purpose: Isolate the effect of prompt predictability on speculative-decoding gains, holding engine, hardware, concurrency and generated-token count constant.
hardware: 2 x a4-highgpu-8g (16 x NVIDIA B200 HGX), RoCEv2, direct container port 8000

arms.name: repeated_passage_prompt
arms.note: Standard run_saturation_sweep_kimi_k3.py prompt: one synthetic passage repeated round(ISL/BASE_TOKENS_APPROX) times.

arms.name: non_repetitive_prompts
arms.note: 16 distinct prompts, coherent English, no passage repeated within or across requests.

finding: Acceptance falls ~2.8x and aggregate throughput 2.53x when the prompt stops being a repeated passage. The Table 4 speedups are a ceiling for repetitive or highly structured traffic.
caveat: The non-speculative baseline could not be re-run on this prompt set before teardown, and these prompts are 46% longer, so 656.60 vs the 492.02 default-profile figure is indicative, not a controlled comparison.
